Using the adjacent intervals rule, we have

$$
{\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t={\int }_{1}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{2}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We can rearrange the above as follows:

$$
{\int }_{1}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t={\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{2}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Finally, using the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{2}^{5}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨-1,\,-3,\,5⟩-⟨9,\,-3,\,-12⟩ \\  & =⟨-10,\,0,\,17⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
